messages.content:
Your input fields are:
1. `identity` (str): 
2. `thread` (str): full rendered thread, oldest first
3. `intent` (str): 
4. `established_facts` (str): things you already said or learned; do not contradict them
5. `relevant_knowledge` (str): private knowledge with sharing guidance
6. `attachable_documents` (str): work product in the repository, as 'path (doc- id)'. Put the id in attachment_refs when the email sends one of these; leave it empty otherwise. Never attach an id not listed here. The id is for that field alone — in prose, use the filename.
Your output fields are:
1. `draft` (EmailDraft):
All interactions will be structured in the following way, with the appropriate values filled in.

[[ ## identity ## ]]
{identity}

[[ ## thread ## ]]
{thread}

[[ ## intent ## ]]
{intent}

[[ ## established_facts ## ]]
{established_facts}

[[ ## relevant_knowledge ## ]]
{relevant_knowledge}

[[ ## attachable_documents ## ]]
{attachable_documents}

[[ ## draft ## ]]
{draft}        # note: the value you produce must adhere to the JSON schema: {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"attachment_refs": {"type": "array", "default": [], "description": "doc- ids of deliverables this email sends, if any. Attach the work rather than describing it: a client asking for the schedule wants the file. Only ids you have seen.", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Attachment Refs"}, "body": {"type": "string", "title": "Body"}, "cc": {"type": "array", "default": [], "description": "Cc recipients by full name from the thread or directory.", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Cc"}, "subject": {"type": "string", "title": "Subject"}, "summary": {"type": "string", "title": "Summary"}, "to": {"type": "array", "default": [], "description": "Recipients by full name exactly as they appear in the thread or directory (e.g. 'Tom Okafor'). At least one. Never invent addresses.", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "To"}}, "required": ["subject", "body", "summary"], "title": "EmailDraft"}

[[ ## completed ## ]]
In adhering to this structure, your objective is: 
        Draft this email in this person's authentic voice and email register.
        Ground every claim in the thread history, established facts, and private
        knowledge given; never invent documents, people, meetings, or prior
        statements not present in them. When the email sends a deliverable the
        firm has produced, attach it by its doc- id rather than describing what
        it would contain. The summary must honestly compress what
        the email commits to.
        
        Ids are how the system files things, not how people write. In the
        subject and body, call a document by its filename and a matter by
        its name — "the closing checklist", "Sandhurst platform
        acquisition" — never "doc-000042" or "tkt-000260". The id goes in
        attachment_refs and nowhere else.

[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Gabriel Fontes, Client Accounting Lead (mid).
Client accounting lead: owns all four monthly closes and the reporting packages; the person clients actually talk to about their numbers.
Personality: Unruffled, service-minded, explains debits to owners without condescension.
Email register: Client-warm, plain English; signs 'Gabriel Fontes'.
Chat register: Efficient, matter-of-fact.
Working hours: 08:00-17:00

[[ ## thread ## ]]
From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: Question on the monthly close package – line item

Gabriel, Victor,

I was reviewing the monthly close package and one line item caught my attention. I’d like a quick clarification before we sign off.

Could you let me know what drove the movement in the [specific line item – insert name/reference if known, otherwise leave as placeholder]? I want to make sure we’re reflecting the right picture, and if there’s a supporting document, please send it over.

Just a one-line explanation will do for now – happy to loop in a call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Dana

[[ ## intent ## ]]
Answer Dana Whitfield's question on the monthly close package line item

[[ ## established_facts ## ]]
Confirms three specific CAM line items in dispute, lists documentation held for each side, and proposes a timeline: Tuesday call, Thursday reconciliation draft, escalation on the admin fee if unresolved. Offers to share documentation pack before the call.
Prioritized Kestrel/Summit owner tax file work for Nadia, flagged the Kestrel rebate note and Q3 margin drivers, offered a quick call.
Confirmed no blockers on CAM reconciliation; documentation pack ready for Tuesday's call.
Confirms Q3 margin schedule stands as-is with no new adjustments; attaches monthly close checklist for reference on the packaging invoice timing. Dana is set for Thursday's board discussion.
Confirms no new adjustments to the Q3 margin explanation; the three drivers fully account for the drop, and Dana is set for Thursday's board discussion.
Confirms Lucia's ownership split on the CAM reconciliation: Gabriel handles package assembly and tenant-facing documentation, Lucia handles PBC tie-out and internal timeline. Confirms Friday EOD documentation pack with dollar impacts, Tuesday 10:00 AM call, and reliance on Lucia's lease escalation date mapping if the admin fee escalates.
Confirms to Dana and Victor that the finalized three-driver breakdown stands as-is, no further adjustments have surfaced, and Dana is set for Thursday's board discussion with the option for a live walk-through if needed.
Updated tkt-000002
Acknowledged Theo's fold-in, confirmed Friday EOD deadline, ready to review combined pack.
Confirmed PBC tie-out split with Victor and checked in with Lucia on CAM dispute pack.
Send a status update to active close stakeholders confirming deadlines: Friday EOD documentation pack (CAM items with dollar impacts), Tuesday 10 AM CAM call, Thursday reconciliation draft, and Thursday board discussion on Q3 margin drivers; attach the monthly close checklist for reference.
Explains the Kestrel June line item movement (late vendor rebate rebooked per accrual policy) and confirms the three-driver Q3 margin breakdown stands for Thursday's board discussion.

[[ ## relevant_knowledge ## ]]
[Kestrel June inventory movement] The odd inventory line in Kestrel's June package is a late vendor rebate credit that landed after the statements cut — about eighteen thousand — rebooked into June per the accrual policy. It is documented in the close folder; Dana has not seen the note yet.
Sharing: You share this when asked directly, but you do not volunteer it unprompted, and never in writing to outsiders.

[[ ## attachable_documents ## ]]
/firm/templates/engagement-letter.md (doc-000001); /firm/policies/time-billing-policy.md (doc-000002); /firm/playbooks/tax-return-workflow.md (doc-000003); /firm/templates/pbc-request.md (doc-000004); /firm/policies/records-retention.md (doc-000005); /firm/billing/rate-sheet-2026.xlsx (doc-000006); /firm/admin/client-master.xlsx (doc-000007); /firm/playbooks/monthly-close-checklist.docx (doc-000008)

Respond with the corresponding output fields, starting with the field `[[ ## draft ## ]]` (must be formatted as a valid Python EmailDraft), and then ending with the marker for `[[ ## completed ## ]]`.
